title: Clara Neupert-Wentz
text:
Research
I study conflict, political violence, and the organization of political authority, particularly where state institutions are uneven, contested, or coexist with other forms of rule. My research asks who exercises authority, how political order is built and maintained, and how these arrangements shape conflict, governance, and our ability to observe both. Current projects investigate:
Conflict data - How violence is reported and measured, how conflict actors shape the information environment, and what disagreement across sources can tell us about violence and measurement uncertainty.
Political authority and conflict - How political authority is organized across state and non-state institutions, and how different configurations of authority shape governance, conflict, and strategies of conflict resolution.
Gender, norms and representation - How kinship systems and local institutions shape women’s political participation, representation, and access to political and legal institutions.
